results.claim: [O'S] Lemma 8.2: gamma(n+j)/gamma(n) < 1.01*(3c^2*log^2 n/16n)^j on 0 <= j <= n^c - n, c > 4/3; provenance said to be the Lambert-W asymptotic of Theorem 1.4.
results.paper_quote: "Lemma 8.2. Suppose c>=1. For n large enough and 0<=j<=n^c-n, we have gamma(n+j)/gamma(n) < 1.01(3c^2 log^2(n)/16n)^j." Proof applies (8.3), derived from Thm 1.4 with K=1, w:=W(2n/pi); the paper then adds "Applying Lemma 8.2 with c=2, (it will become apparent that any c>=4/3 will do)".
results.doc_quote: "The engine is the moment-ratio bound (Lemma 8.2, from the Lambert-W asymptotic of Theorem 1.4): gamma(n+j)/gamma(n) < 1.01.(3c^2.log^2n/16n)^j on 0 <= j <= n^c - n, c > 4/3"; notes: "the constants audit says 'c = 2'; both readings are reproduced as printed".
results.notes: Number, statement, constant 1.01 and the 3c^2/16 shape all match, as does the stated provenance (Thm 1.4 with K=1). The hypothesis differs by version: v1 states "Suppose c>0", v2 (the version the Status cites) states "Suppose c>=1"; the document's "c > 4/3" is strictly inside both, and is exactly the paper's own remark that any c>=4/3 will do, so the domain is narrowed, never widened. The doc's own Notes flag this. Range n^c-n and the parameter j are otherwise verbatim.

results.claim: [O'S] Theorem 1.1: RH true iff J_{d,n}(X) is hyperbolic for all d >= 1, n >= 0, with J_{d,n}(X) = sum C(d,j) gamma(n+j) X^j as [O'S] (1.3).
results.paper_quote: "Theorem 1.1. The Riemann hypothesis is true if and only if J^{d,n}(X) is hyperbolic for all d>=1, n>=0." and "J^{d,n}(X):=sum_{j=0}^{d} binom(d,j) gamma(n+j) X^{j}. (1.3)"
results.doc_quote: "**[O'S] Theorem 1.1.** *The Riemann hypothesis is true if and only if J_{d,n}(X) is hyperbolic for all d >= 1, n >= 0.*" with "J_{d,n}(X) = Sum_{j=0}^{d} C(d,j).gamma(n+j).X^j ([O'S] (1.3) = POSITIVITY (13))".
results.notes: Statement and both quantifier axes (all d>=1, all n>=0) are verbatim; equation (1.3) matches. Numbering is the same in v1 and v2. Notation only: the paper writes the superscript J^{d,n}(X) in (1.3)/Thm 1.1 while the document writes J_{d,n}(X); the paper itself uses J^{d,n} and J_{d,n} interchangeably in the Sect. 3 proofs, so no content is changed. The companion citation of Corollary 3.2 (Theta^{(n)} hyperbolic iff J^{d,n} hyperbolic for all d>=1) is also correct.

results.claim: [O'S] Theorem 1.2: RH true iff P_{d,n}(X) is hyperbolic for all d >= 1, n >= 0, with P_{d,n}(X) = sum C(d,j) gamma(n+j) H_{d-j}(X) as [O'S] (1.4).
results.paper_quote: "Theorem 1.2. The Riemann hypothesis is true if and only if P^{d,n}(X) is hyperbolic for all d>=1, n>=0." and "P^{d,n}(X):=sum_{j=0}^{d} binom(d,j) gamma(n+j) H_{d-j}(X). (1.4)"
results.doc_quote: "**[O'S] Theorem 1.2.** *The Riemann hypothesis is true if and only if P_{d,n}(X) is hyperbolic for all d >= 1, n >= 0.*" with "P_{d,n}(X) = Sum_{j=0}^{d} C(d,j).gamma(n+j).H_{d-j}(X)".
results.notes: Statement, quantifiers and the family (1.4) match verbatim. The paper's (3.6) writes the same family as P^{d,n}(x/2) with H_{d-j}(x/2), i.e. the argument rescaled by 2; that is an internal renaming in the paper (P^{d,n}(X) = P^{d,n}(X/2) up to the x -> x/2 substitution, and hyperbolicity is invariant under it), so the document's use of (1.4) is the paper's own definition. Same superscript/subscript notation difference as Theorem 1.1; numbering identical in v1 and v2.

results.claim: [O'S] Theorem 1.3: for all d sufficiently large, P_{d,n}(X) is hyperbolic whenever n/log^2 n >= d^{3/4}/2.
results.paper_quote: "Theorem 1.3. For all d sufficiently large, P^{d,n}(X) is hyperbolic whenever n/log^2 n >= d^{3/4}/2."
results.doc_quote: "**[O'S] Theorem 1.3.** *For all d sufficiently large, P_{d,n}(X) is hyperbolic whenever n/log^2 n >= d^{3/4}/2.*" with "'d sufficiently large' is part of the statement; the threshold is n/log^2 n >= d^{3/4}/2."
results.notes: Verbatim; the 'for all d sufficiently large' qualifier is retained, not dropped, and the threshold constant /2 is retained. (v1 and v2 number this identically.) One imprecision in the document's accounting, not in the theorem: the paper derives the sufficient condition (9d log^4 n/32n^2)^2 <= 3/d, i.e. n/log^2 n >= (27/1024)^{1/4} d^{3/4} = 0.403 d^{3/4}, which is stronger than the stated d^{3/4}/2 = 0.5 d^{3/4}; the source's gloss 'The /2 in the theorem is (27/1024)^{1/4} = 0.403 rounded generously' reads the rounding in the loose direction. The theorem as quoted is what the paper says, so the claim stands.

results.claim: [O'S] Theorem 3.5: for Phi(z) = sum c_j z^j/j! real entire of genus 1* and Omega in the Laguerre-Polya class, Phi is hyperbolic iff the polynomials sum C(d,j) c_j g*_{d-j}(Omega;x) (3.5) are hyperbolic for all d >= 1.
results.paper_quote: "Theorem 3.5. Let Phi(z)=sum_{j=0}^{infty} c_{j}z^{j}/j! be a real entire function of genus 1^{*} and let Omega(z) be in the Laguerre-Polya class. Then Phi(z) is hyperbolic if and only if the polynomials sum_{j=0}^{d} binom(d,j)c_{j}.g^{*}_{d-j}(Omega;x) (3.5) are hyperbolic for all d>=1."
results.doc_quote: "**[O'S] Theorem 3.5.** *Let Phi(z) = Sum_{j>=0} c_j.z^j/j! be a real entire function of genus 1* and let Omega(z) be in the Laguerre-Polya class. Then Phi(z) is hyperbolic if and only if the polynomials Sum_{j=0}^{d} C(d,j) . c_j . g*_{d-j}(Omega; x) (3.5) are hyperbolic for all d >= 1.*"
results.notes: Verbatim match of hypotheses (genus 1*, real entire), of the equivalence, of display (3.5) and of the quantifier 'for all d>=1'; numbering identical in v1 and v2. Minor: the document writes the hypothesis as bare 'Omega in the LP class' whereas the paper writes 'Omega in LP_{>=0}' (the subscript >=0 records that the function is >=0 on the real axis) -- a standard part of the LP class definition, not a dropped substantive condition. The document's dial readings (Omega=1 -> J; Omega=e^{-z^2} -> P via g*_d(e^{-z^2};x)=H_d(x/2); Omega=Bessel -> Laguerre) are all stated in the paper's Sect. 3.2-3.3.

results.claim: [O'S] Theorem 3.9: RH true iff Q_{d,n,nu}(x) = sum C(d+nu,j) gamma(n+j) x^j L^{(nu)}_{d-j}(x) are hyperbolic for all d >= 1, all n >= 0 and all real nu > -2.
results.paper_quote: "Theorem 3.9. The Riemann hypothesis is true if and only if the polynomials Q^{d,n,alpha}(x):=sum_{j=0}^{d} binom(d+alpha,j) gamma(n+j)x^{j}L^{(alpha)}_{d-j}(x) are hyperbolic for all d>=1, all n>=0 and all real alpha>=-2." (alpha > -2 is NOT what the paper says; the paper says alpha >= -2.)
results.doc_quote: "**[O'S] Theorem 3.9.** *The Riemann hypothesis is true if and only if the polynomials Q_{d,n,nu}(x) := Sum_{j=0}^{d} C(d+nu, j).gamma(n+j).x^j.L^(nu)_{d-j}(x) are hyperbolic for all d >= 1, all n >= 0 and all real nu > -2.*"
results.notes: The parameter range attributed to the paper is wrong. The paper's Theorem 3.9 reads 'all real alpha >= -2' (closed), in BOTH v1 and v2, and the paper's own worked d=2 case confirms the endpoint is intended: the discriminant is given as (alpha+2)gamma(n)^2+(alpha+1)^2(alpha+2)^2[gamma(n+1)^2-gamma(n)gamma(n+2)], 'non-negative if alpha>=-2'. The document (and its source file) states nu > -2, excluding the endpoint alpha=-2 that the paper includes, and presents it as the verbatim theorem. The polynomial family Q^{d,n,alpha}, the quantifiers d>=1 and n>=0, and the attribution to the Bessel dial J_alpha are all correct; only the range is misquoted/shifted.

results.claim: Turan's Theorem III, quoted as [O'S] Theorem 8.1: a Hermite combination G = sum c_j H_j has real simple zeros when sum_{j=0}^{d-2} 2^j j! c_j^2 < 2^d (d-1)! c_d^2 (8.1).
results.paper_quote: "Theorem 8.1. Let G(z)=sum_{j=0}^{d} c_{j}H_{j}(z) for real numbers c_{j} and H_{j}(z) the j th Hermite polynomial. Then the zeros of G(z) are real and simple when sum_{j=0}^{d-2}2^{j}j!c_{j}^{2}<2^{d}(d-1)!c_{d}^{2}. (8.1)" -- introduced as "due to Turan from [Tur59, Thm. III]"; then "The condition (8.1) for P^{d,n}(X) to be hyperbolic, with c_{j}=binom(d,j)gamma(n+d-j), is sum_{j=2}^{d} d/(2^{j}j!) binom(d,j) gamma(n+j)^{2}/gamma(n)^{2}<1. (8.2)"
results.doc_quote: "Both proofs certify hyperbolicity with the same tool, Turan's Theorem III ([O'S] Theorem 8.1): a Hermite combination G = Sum c_j.H_j has real simple zeros when Sum_{j=0}^{d-2} 2^j.j!.c_j^2 < 2^d.(d-1)!.c_d^2. (8.1)" with "(8.1) => (8.2): with c_j = C(d,j).gamma(n+d-j), the weight is (d-j)!.C(d,j)^2/(2^j.(d-1)!) = d.C(d,j)/(2^j.j!)."
results.notes: Criterion, the 'real and simple' conclusion and the constants all match (8.1) exactly; the attribution to Turan's Thm III is the paper's own ('This is based on the next result, due to Turan from [Tur59, Thm. III]'). The displayed (8.2) and the weight identity (d-j)!C(d,j)^2/(2^j(d-1)!) = d C(d,j)/(2^j j!) are also correct as printed in the proof of Theorem 1.3. Numbering identical in v1 and v2.
